title: Snack packaging study, freshness perception
hook: More than half of people have thrown away a snack that wasn't actually spoiled.
insight_paragraph: 54% of respondents said they'd tossed a partially finished packet of a snack in the last month because it felt stale, without even tasting it first. The product wasn't spoiled. The packaging just made them think it was. A meaningful share of what brands call category waste isn't a shelf life problem. It's a perception problem, and it's driven entirely by how a pack looks and feels once it's been opened. We ran a study on 1,240 verified respondents across metros and tier two cities to find out exactly how much packaging format alone shapes that perception, independent of what's actually inside the pack.
supporting_points: 71% said a resealable pack alone made them feel a snack was fresher, even when told the product inside was identical to a foil pack.
This held across every income bracket. Respondents in the lowest bracket trusted resealable packaging just as much as those in the highest, 68% versus 73%.
44% said they'd pay more for a resealable pack, with a median acceptable premium of 8%.
Health conscious respondents were no more likely to value resealability than anyone else. This is a mainstream preference, not a niche one.
When shown two identical snacks side by side, one in foil and one in a resealable pouch, 62% picked the resealable one as the pack they'd choose again.
closing_line: The next packaging call your brand makes might do more for perceived freshness than anything happening inside the pack.
source_study: Snack Packaging Preferences, Urban India, Sept 2026
hero_stat_label: tossed a snack that wasn't spoiled, without even tasting it
